name: Field guidance — placeholders, descriptions and input purpose

generated.generator: authored (batch 3, from the 2026-08-10 blinded visual check backlog)

summary.value: How a form field tells the user what to enter: guidance before the field, never placeholder-only; descriptions (help text) for difficult content such as expected formats; autocomplete attributes where the field's purpose is predefined.

value.name: Textfield
value.role: carries label, description and error in one composition

value.name: Field
value.role: links label, description, validation message and counter for assistive technology

a11y.method: drafted from the docs pages, quote-verified 2026-08-12, human review pending (batch 3)

value.rule: Avoid guidance text inside the input itself (placeholders); give all relevant information before the user fills in the field
value.quote: Users should not have to try and fail, so give them all relevant information before they choose an option or fill in a field. Avoid guidance text inside the input itself, also known as placeholders. Placeholders disappear when the field is filled in, and may conflict with accessibility requirements.

value.rule: Autocomplete is required on fields with a predefined purpose
value.quote: Autocomplete is required in fields where a predefined purpose exists, as defined in 1.3.5

value.rule: Use a description (help text) to explain difficult content — legal terms, specialist language, expected formats
value.quote: Sometimes descriptions, also known as help text, are useful for explaining something difficult, such as legal terms or specialist language.

value.rule: Only use descriptions where needed, to reduce cognitive load
value.quote: Only use descriptions where they are needed, to reduce cognitive load.
